title: The Sealed Finding
protagonist: Josiah Motaung, Director of the Directorate of Preventive Enforcement
logline: The man who built a state that arrests people for murders they have not yet committed is named by his own machine — and the report that would clear him is sealed in a drawer, alongside the proof that both reports are true.
blueprint: Philip K. Dick, The Minority Report (1956) engine: precrime bureau; the founder named by his own system; the successor he wrongly fears; the faction that wants the bureau dead; the sealed dissent; the recursion of sequential futures; the deliberate murder that makes the machine true. Precognition replaced by inference; original cast, world, institutions and prose.
market: literary near-future crime / procedural SF / state-power tragedy: craft exercise, not for commercial release
lineage: Philip K. Dick, 'The Minority Report' (Fantastic Universe, January 1956)
setting: Near-now South Africa (Gauteng: Pretoria, Johannesburg, the East Rand), c. 2050s
sensitivity_read: RECOMMENDED — preventive detention in a country with a living memory of detention without trial; the named are disproportionately poor. See canon/MYTHOS.md and the all-sides law.
